title: Logic learning machine derives explainable genetic-risk rules for biliary cholangitis
summary: A logic learning machine trained on GWAS-significant variants in 1345 individuals (444 cases) generated 38 if-then rules for primary biliary cholangitis risk. The best model had accuracy 71.7%, sensitivity 0.28 and specificity 0.93, and an AUC of 0.73 in an independent validation cohort of 834. Discrimination is modest and sensitivity low.
ai_technology: Logic Learning Machine generating if-then rules from genotype data
organization: Department of Medicine and Surgery, University of Milano-Bicocca, Monza, Italy; Rulex Innovation Labs, Genoa, Italy

evidence.tested: Rule-based classification from known GWAS variants, validated in a separate Italian cohort.
evidence.unknown: Clinical usefulness given low sensitivity, and performance beyond the cohorts studied; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A logic learning machine selected variants and produced explainable rules for disease classification.
